    2. The assessment questionnaire must reach assessment team members 3 days prior to
         assessment in order for all members to study the document. The assessment team must
         consist of at least the following:

    ● One committee member responsible for the administration of the visit.
    ● A minimum of two “peer members”– a “peer member” is a farmer/producer who is a

         member of a PGS and has knowledge or understanding of the production on the
         farm/production being assessed.
    ● One “public” member – a customer or independent retailer who would normally consume
         and/or purchase the product/s from the assessed farm.
    ● Should none of the group members hold the specific knowledge required for a farm visited,
         a technical expert should be included in the group.

    3. Once the administrator has received all the above documentation, it will be forwarded to
         members of the assessment team.

4.2 Assessment:

    1) The committee member responsible for the administration of the farm visit will be
         responsible for completing the assessment report and will “drive” the process.

    2) All participants on the farm visit will complete the “Farm visit checklist”
    3) All members have the right to ask questions and can explore any query that might have

         arisen out of the supplied documentation prior to the assessment.
    4) A walkthrough of the farm/production premises will be conducted and Q&A will take place

         during this walkthrough.
    5) After the walkthrough, all comments, suggestions or further queries will be handled in a

         short meeting before discussing the assessment. This meeting is an open forum. All
         participants will be expected to give their comments openly at this meeting. A
         prospective applicant has the right to hear these comments first hand and will be given
         the opportunity to respond to or clarify any misunderstanding. The aim is to limit further
         off-premises or long-distance discussion to the absolute minimum. Ideally, the
         assessment process should be finalised up to the provisional acceptance stage at that
         meeting. But in some instances, when the members are not able to come to a
         conclusion, further investigation may be required. This should be completed and
         members of the visiting committee should come to conclusion on the assessment no
         later than 5 days after the farm visit.
    6) Results will be collated, further verification conducted (if necessary) and actions and/or
         remedies requested.
    7) Timelines for all the above must be recorded.
    8) As soon as the applicant has complied with these requests, all results will be collated and
         a final report completed/submitted.
    9) Farmer members who have taken part in the visit will be asked to share insights and scope
         for improving practices in a peer review analysis to be collated to the final report.
    10) The committee will review the approval documentation at their quarterly meetings
    11) All documentation regarding the assessment will be filed and administered by the
         Outeniqua PGS administrator.
    12) Traceability: Retailer and market members or farmer members selling their own produce
         shall ensure that an invoicing/delivery note system is in place to ensure an audit trail from
         farm to marketplace. This must be accessible to the committee as part of quality
         management and be available for the resolution of queries or complaints.
